blocks.text: Imagine you have a task that you need to perform multiple times in your code. Instead of writing the same code repeatedly, you can define a function to encapsulate this task. This not only makes your code cleaner but also easier to manage and debug.

blocks.markdown: In programming, a function is a named section of a code that performs a specific task. Functions allow us to encapsulate code for reuse, abstraction, and modularity. In this lesson, we'll explore how to define a function with parameters and return values, and how to call it correctly.

blocks.title: Function
blocks.text: A function is a block of organized, reusable code that performs a single, related action.

blocks.markdown:
### Defining a Function
To define a function, you need to specify its name, parameters, and the code block it will execute. In Python, this is done using the `def` keyword.

blocks.caption: Basic structure of a function definition in Python.

blocks.markdown:
### Example
Consider a function that calculates the square of a number. We define it as follows:

blocks.title: Defining a Simple Function
blocks.prompt: Define a function `square` that takes one parameter and returns its square.

steps.text: Start by using the `def` keyword followed by the function name `square`.
Specify the parameter inside the parentheses: `def square(x):`.
Inside the function, return the square of the parameter: `return x * x`.

blocks.markdown:
### Calling a Function
Once a function is defined, you can call it by using its name followed by parentheses enclosing any arguments.

blocks.title: Calling a Function
blocks.prompt: Call the `square` function with the argument 3.

steps.text: Write the function name followed by parentheses: `square()`.
Place the argument inside the parentheses: `square(3)`.
The function returns the value `9`, which is the square of 3.

blocks.title: Function Contract
blocks.text: A function's contract consists of its preconditions (what must be true before the function is called) and postconditions (what the function guarantees after it is called).

blocks.markdown:
### Parameters and Arguments
Parameters are variables listed in a function's definition, while arguments are the data you pass into the function's parameters when you call it.

### Pass-by-Value vs Pass-by-Reference
In programming, the way arguments are passed to functions can be either by value or by reference. Understanding this distinction is crucial for predicting how changes to parameters affect the original data.

blocks.title: Pass-by-Value
blocks.text: In pass-by-value, a copy of the argument's value is made in memory. Changes to the parameter within the function do not affect the original argument.

blocks.title: Pass-by-Reference
blocks.text: In pass-by-reference, a reference to the actual data is passed. Changes to the parameter within the function affect the original argument.

points: Functions encapsulate code for reuse and abstraction.
Define functions with a name, parameters, and a return value.
Understand the difference between pass-by-value and pass-by-reference.
